nodes.label: ai-layout-integrity
nodes.summary: The repository's AI layer is real: the manifest declares a format this executable reads and every section it names exists, the checkout-local half is ignored by git and nothing under it is tracked, and no project data remains under the pre-.ai .majordomus/ path.

nodes.label: checkpoint-freshness
nodes.summary: A task whose last checkpoint is older than its profile's interval is reported, not stopped.

nodes.label: layout-integrity
nodes.summary: The directories the durable commands write into are installed rather than created on first use.

nodes.label: ledger-integrity
nodes.summary: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event; the one durable record nothing else can reconstruct stays readable.

nodes.label: policy-completeness
nodes.summary: Every policy value the code reads is declared in the skeleton policy, and no reader carries its own default for one.

nodes.label: bootstrap-integrity
nodes.summary: The path from a human reader to the AI layer is unbroken — README.md names AGENTS.md, every generated instruction file points at .ai/README.md, and none of them carries a rule of its own.

nodes.label: catalogue-integrity
nodes.summary: Every use case and application describes the tool in terms the tool has — each command, doctrine and claim it names exists, and the two catalogues reference each other in both directions.

nodes.label: context-integrity
nodes.summary: Every directory of the AI layer carries a context document, each one carries the contract, they compose into one deterministic chain for every path, and a tree that does not validate resolves nothing.

nodes.label: policy-integrity
nodes.summary: The policy and every profile parse, declare version 1, and carry no key the schema does not define.

nodes.label: adr-integrity
nodes.summary: Every architecture decision the repository holds parses against the decision contract, claims an identity nothing else claims, and every relation and reference it makes resolves.

nodes.label: blocker-resolution
nodes.summary: No task can be completed while any question on this branch is unresolved; it can still be finished as blocked, partial, no_match or failed.

nodes.label: decision-records
nodes.summary: Every entry in decisions.md carries the task, the head and the reason, so a decision can be found by the worker who needs it.

nodes.label: dag-integrity
nodes.summary: The issue dependency graph is acyclic, every edge names an issue that exists, and no issue is executing ahead of a dependency that is not done.

nodes.label: command-surface
nodes.summary: Every command the binary dispatches is described by the shipped registry, every command the registry declares public is dispatched, and a command is public exactly when the usage text lists it.

nodes.label: doctrine-wiring-integrity
nodes.summary: Every doctrine in this registry resolves to a validator that exists, is reached from every command it names, propagates failure, is proved by a test, and is run by CI — and every validator in the source is declared here.

nodes.label: enforcement-wiring
nodes.summary: Every enforcement the policy declares is invoked by the hook it names, from a file the dispatcher will actually execute, without swallowing the exit code.

nodes.label: command-coverage
nodes.summary: Every public command has a behavioural test and a negative test, computed from the registry and the coverage each case declares about itself rather than from a list someone maintains.

nodes.label: handover-integrity
nodes.summary: The resolver runs and reports either the record for this worktree and branch or its clean absence; a malformed record is never silently skipped, and a record describing a history this checkout no longer has is reported.

nodes.label: note-integrity
nodes.summary: Every outcome needs a note carrying the sections that outcome requires, and no transcript.

nodes.label: profile-requirements
nodes.summary: A profile may demand more than the shared contract — a regression test, a decision record — and finish refuses without it.

nodes.label: project-integrity
nodes.summary: Every milestone and issue file parses, carries the id its filename claims, and contains no key nobody reads.

nodes.label: projection-integrity
nodes.summary: Every generated instruction file exists, matches the stamp it carries, and is never silently overwritten after a hand edit.

nodes.label: context-budget
nodes.summary: The always-loaded projection stays within its line budget, every reference in it resolves, it states no count that will go stale, and the assembled context fits the builder's own budget.

nodes.label: deployment-contract
nodes.summary: A deployment of the executable is a canonical object of the layer against a closed contract; the container definition and the provider configuration are projections of it, never a second description.

nodes.label: prompt-capture
nodes.summary: A repository that declares prompt capture has it wired below the model and proven by running it; the archive stays ignored and untracked, every prompt is present as both a record and a rendering, and neither carries anything the model said.

nodes.label: prompt-continuity
nodes.summary: Every captured prompt names the episode it belongs to or says why it cannot; the archive is readable by its owner alone, bounded by a declared retention policy, and never holds credential material verbatim.

nodes.label: prompt-integrity
nodes.summary: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and every token in it is one the renderer knows.

nodes.label: questions-store-integrity
nodes.summary: Every entry in open-questions.md parses, because a gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one.

nodes.label: retention-caps
nodes.summary: The ledger and the handover directory stay under the caps the policy sets, so durable state does not grow without bound.

nodes.label: roadmap-integrity
nodes.summary: No document is a second authority for the roadmap. While a hand-written roadmap table exists, it can neither list a version no milestone declares nor hide one the model does.

nodes.label: rule-package-integrity
nodes.summary: The repository's effective rule set is real: the vendored baseline matches its manifest file for file, every rule resolves with its dependencies and no two claim one identity, and no project rule reuses the vendored namespace.

nodes.label: schema-integrity
nodes.summary: The order the rules apply in is written down rather than left in the code; every kind the tool reads declares a schema, every schema is named by a kind, and every path under the repository's AI layer is claimed by a source so that nothing is carried through unvalidated.

nodes.label: scope-integrity
nodes.summary: A task touches only the paths it claimed; work found elsewhere is not accepted as done.

nodes.label: session-records
nodes.summary: A closed execution episode is written once, into the layer's sessions section, against a schema that admits what the repository can prove and nothing else.

nodes.label: session-lifecycle
nodes.summary: Where a provider fires session events, the episode is opened and closed by that provider's hook rather than by the model, the start event hands the worker the bounded briefing the policy declares, and the working context each open freezes stays under the ignored half of the layer, carries the declared keys, and never carries a conversation.

nodes.label: skill-integrity
nodes.summary: Every skill the repository declares parses against the skill contract, names the directory it lives in, carries its sections, describes itself in terms no other skill uses, and every skill or example it refers to exists.

nodes.label: state-consistency
nodes.summary: The task record still describes this checkout — same branch, and HEAD at or ahead of the recorded commit.

nodes.label: task-continuity
nodes.summary: A task finished as partial or blocked should leave a handover record, not only a note section.

nodes.label: use-case-coverage
nodes.summary: Every public command, and every guaranteed claim and MCP tool the policy asks for, is named and run by at least one active use case whose scenario executes against the real tool; a gap is a failure or a report according to the policy, never silence.

nodes.label: verification-integrity
nodes.summary: Completion requires a verification command that actually ran and exited 0; its exit code and duration are recorded.

nodes.label: obligation-closure
nodes.summary: A task that declares obligations reaches the outcome completed only when each one is established by the tool or has evidence, and that evidence still describes the tree or the commit it was taken over.
